listenings.text: Hi Rodrigo, it's Claire. I read your contingency plan. It is very good. One question: if the ship from Madagascar is late in December, will you have enough stock for Christmas? If you need vanilla from France, call me, and I will talk to the plant in Grasse. If we act early, there won't be a problem. Speak soon.

Good morning. Here is the weather for New York this weekend. On Saturday it will be sunny and cool. On Sunday there will be rain in the afternoon. If you go to Central Park on Sunday, go in the morning. And if you go out at night, take a jacket: it will be cold.

extra_audio.text: The ship with the vanilla left Madagascar. There was a storm at sea, so the ship was late. Rodrigo opened the contingency plan. It said: if the ship is late, we will use the stock in France. The vanilla from France arrived, and the customer was happy.

reading.rtitle: Contingency Plan -- Vanilla Imports, Fourth Quarter
paras: Every year, the plant in Brazil imports vanilla from Madagascar by ship. The containers arrive at the port of Santos. This plan shows the main risks for the fourth quarter, and what the team will do.
Risk 1: a storm at sea. If there is a storm, the ship will be late. If the ship is more than ten days late, we will use our backup plan: vanilla from the stock in France.
Risk 2: a strike at the port. If there is a strike in Santos, the containers will stay at the port. In that case, we will send the next containers to the port of Rio.
Risk 3: an urgent customer order. If a customer needs vanilla in less than a week, we will use air freight. It is expensive, so the director will approve it first.
Rule for everybody. If you see a new risk, tell the planning team the same day.
